q: What is the carbon footprint of Ahmedabad's chemical units in Vatva, Naroda and Odhav, and how does one unit compare?
title: Ahmedabad chemical units: carbon footprint
short: A typical dyes and pigments unit in Vatva uses about 532 toe a year, close to 1,540 t CO2, nearly three-quarters of it from natural gas. Across Ahmedabad's 750 chemical units, TERI's BEE study counted 144,624 toe in 2020-21, roughly 488,000 t CO2 at today's factors (estimate).
audience: Dye, dye intermediate and chemical units in GIDC Vatva, Naroda and Odhav

sections.h: The cluster, by estate and fuel
p: About 600 units in Vatva, 100 in Naroda and 50 in Odhav. Around 80% make dyes and dye intermediates, and about 76% are small units producing 200 to 600 tonnes a year.

In 2020-21 the cluster burnt 121 million scm of natural gas, 18,000 t of coal and 10,800 t of biomass, and bought 308 million kWh. Gas fires the boilers, thermic fluid heaters and hot air generators for dryers; some micro and small units still burn wood or coal.

ul: Unit sizes in the study run from 15.1 to 2,080.6 toe a year.
Typical dyes and pigments unit: 478.2 toe of heat and 53.6 toe of electricity, 531.8 toe in all.
Typical other-chemicals unit: 129 toe of heat and 52.8 toe of electricity, 181.8 toe.
Heat is 89.2% of energy across the units studied, so the dryer and the boiler set your number.

sections.h: What a tonne of dye carries
p: Divide your year's CO2 by tonnes produced. A small unit at 400 t a year with the typical dyes profile would carry close to 3.9 t CO2 per tonne from its own energy, before the raw materials it buys. Drying in tray and spin flash dryers takes 20 to 36 hours a batch, the longest and one of the most heat-hungry steps, so start looking there.

sections.h: Who asks, and why CBAM is not it
p: Dyes, pigments and most organic chemicals are not CBAM goods. The requests come from customers: textile and leather processors counting their purchased chemicals, multinational buyers asking for a product carbon footprint per kg, and lenders financing a boiler or dryer upgrade.

sections.h: Where the study says to cut
ul: Feed-water preheating from boiler flue gas, and air-to-fuel control on thermic fluid heaters.
Temperature-based control on spray dryer fans and feed pumps.
Timers on reactors and ball mills to stop idle running, IE3 motors in place of rewound ones, and rooftop solar.
Monthly gas bills in scm and electricity bills in kWh.
Coal or wood invoices by weight if you use any.
Batch register with kg produced per product, so shared steam can be split by batch.

example.title: Estimate: one typical dyes and pigments unit for a year
lines: Heat: 478.2 toe x 10 million kcal / 8,750 kcal per scm = 546,500 scm of gas
Electricity: 53.6 toe at the study's 860 kcal per kWh = 623,300 kWh x 0.675 = 421 t CO2
Cluster: gas 121 million scm x 2.05 = 248,050 t; coal 18,000 t x 1.76 = 31,680 t; power 308 million kWh x 0.675 = 207,900 t; about 487,630 t
example.note: Assumes all heat is gas, using the study's 8,750 kcal per scm and Senseible's default factors with the FY 2025-26 grid factor. Biomass CO2 is reported separately and left out. Your bills give your figure.

senseible: Senseible reads your gas and electricity bills into a dated Scope 1 and 2 record with the factor behind each line; add tonnes produced and you have the per-tonne figure a customer or lender asks for.
